panresizer.content.heading1: What is a PAN Card Document Resizer?
panresizer.content.p1: A PAN card document resizer is a specialized online image tool designed to help applicants prepare scans or digital photographs of their Permanent Account Number (PAN) card for online portal submissions. Online application systems, government registration forms, banking portals, and identity verification services often enforce strict file size limits (such as under 20 KB, 50 KB, or 100 KB) and specific pixel dimensions. This tool allows you to adjust both pixel resolution and KB file size so your document meets any portal's exact upload rules.
panresizer.content.heading2: How to Resize a PAN Card Image for Online Upload
panresizer.content.p2: Preparing a PAN card photo for online submission requires balancing file size with visual legibility. Follow these simple steps:
panresizer.content.step1: 1. Upload your cropped PAN card photo by dragging it into the upload box or selecting it from your device.
panresizer.content.step2: 2. Choose your preferred resize mode: Dimensions (px), Percentage, or Target File Size (KB).
panresizer.content.step3: 3. For target file size requirements, select a preset like 20 KB, 50 KB, or 100 KB, or enter a custom KB value.
panresizer.content.step4: 4. For exact dimensions, enter your target Width and Height in pixels while keeping aspect ratio locked.
panresizer.content.step5: 5. Click 'Resize Image' and inspect the preview to ensure all text, card numbers, and signatures remain sharp and clear.
panresizer.content.step6: 6. Download your optimized PAN card image instantly to your phone or computer.
panresizer.content.heading3: How to Reduce PAN Card Image Size in KB
panresizer.content.p3: When uploading documents to online portals, the most common error is exceeding the maximum allowed file size. High-resolution smartphone cameras take photos ranging from 3 MB to 10 MB, whereas most upload portals cap document attachments at 20 KB to 200 KB. Our Target File Size mode uses iterative binary-search compression algorithms to reduce file size intelligently while preserving text readability and document clarity.
panresizer.content.heading4: Dimensions vs File Size: Understanding the Difference
panresizer.content.p4: Pixel dimensions (e.g., 600 × 400 pixels) determine how wide and tall the image renders on a screen or in a document viewer. File size in KB (Kilobytes) measures how much storage space the file occupies on disk. Reducing pixel dimensions inherently decreases file size, but adjusting image compression quality allows you to achieve smaller KB sizes without shrinking the document's physical layout.
panresizer.content.heading5: Choosing the Right Specifications for Your Application
panresizer.content.p5: Different portals, banks, and registration forms set different technical requirements. Always check the official upload guidelines for your specific application form. Rather than enforcing fixed constraints, ImgFeel gives you total flexibility to enter any custom width, height, or target KB size required by your portal.
panresizer.content.p6: A compressed PAN card image must remain 100% legible. Verification officers and automated OCR systems need to clearly read your 10-digit alphanumeric PAN number, full name, date of birth, and view your photo and signature without blurriness. Avoid over-compressing images below 15 KB if text becomes grainy or unreadable.
panresizer.content.heading7: Supported Image Formats: JPG, PNG, and WebP
panresizer.content.p7: JPG (or JPEG) is the standard format accepted by almost all online document submission portals due to its efficient compression. PNG offers lossless clarity, ideal for crisp text, while WebP provides ultra-modern compression. ImgFeel supports all three formats seamlessly.
panresizer.content.p8: A PAN card is a sensitive national tax identity document containing your full name, father's name, birth date, and permanent identification number. Unlike traditional online converters that upload your personal documents to cloud servers, ImgFeel executes all image processing 100% locally inside your web browser. Your private document never leaves your phone or computer, protecting you completely against data leaks and unauthorized server storage.
panresizer.content.heading9: Common PAN Card Photo Upload Mistakes
panresizer.content.p9: Avoid these frequent mistakes when preparing your PAN card image:
panresizer.content.mistake1: Uploading Uncropped Photos: Uploading a full table or background with a small PAN card in the center wastes file size and leads to rejection. Crop your image closely around the card borders first.
panresizer.content.mistake2: Unreadable Numbers or Text: Over-compressing to hit an unnecessarily tiny file size can smudge the PAN number or QR code. Aim for the highest size allowed under the portal limit.
panresizer.content.mistake3: Distorted Aspect Ratio: Stretching a rectangular PAN card into a square box distorts the photo and signature. Keep aspect ratio locked during resizing.
panresizer.faq.q1: How do I resize a PAN card photo under 20 KB?
panresizer.faq.a1: Upload your PAN card image, select 'Target Size (KB)', click the '20 KB' preset button (or enter 20 KB), and click 'Resize Image'. The browser automatically optimizes compression to generate a file under 20 KB.
panresizer.faq.q2: Is it safe to resize my PAN card photo online with ImgFeel?
panresizer.faq.a2: Yes, 100% safe. ImgFeel processes all images entirely inside your browser using client-side JavaScript. Your PAN card photo is never uploaded to any server or stored online.
panresizer.faq.q3: What is the ideal resolution for PAN card image uploads?
panresizer.faq.a3: Requirements vary by portal. Most portals accept width between 400 to 800 pixels and file size between 20 KB to 200 KB. Always verify your specific portal instructions.
panresizer.faq.q4: Can I resize a PAN card image on my mobile phone?
panresizer.faq.a4: Yes. ImgFeel is fully responsive and optimized for smartphone browsers. You can take a photo of your PAN card with your phone camera, upload it directly, and resize it instantly.
